chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi, from al-Abbas ibn Amir, from Ahmad ibn Zarq, from Yahya ibn Abi al-'Ala', from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, a servant was dwelling in the Fire for seventy autumns - and one autumn is seventy years - He said: Then, indeed, he asked Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'By Muhammad and his Household, have mercy upon me.'
He said: Then Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, revealed to Jibra'eel (peace be upon him): 'Descend unto My servant and let him out.'
He said: 'O Lord, how can I descend into the Fire?' He said: 'Indeed, I have ordered it to be, for you, coolness and peace.'
He said: 'O Lord, I have no knowledge of his location.' He said: 'Indeed, he is in a pit of Sijjeen.'
He said: Then he descended into the Fire and found him roped on his face.
He said: Then he took him out to Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, and He said: 'O My servant, how much did you dwell calling to Me in the Fire?'
He said: 'I do not count, O Lord.'

He said: 'Verily, by My Might, were it not for what you asked Me with, I would have prolonged your ignominy in the Fire. However, it is a necessity upon Myself that no servant asks Me by Muhammad and his Household, except that I forgive him for what was between Me and him, and I have forgiven you today.'

key_terms.بِحَقِّ مُحَمَّدٍ وَأَهْلِ بَيْتِهِ: by the right of Muhammad and his Household
key_terms.حَتَّمْتُ عَلَى نَفْسِي: I made it obligatory upon Myself
key_terms.سِجِّينٍ: Sijjeen (a specific pit or layer in Hell)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of asking Allah by the right of Muhammad and his Household for forgiveness in Hellfire?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Mani al-Akhbar* illustrates the Shia doctrine of *Shafa'ah* (intercession) and the efficacy of invoking the *Haqq* (right/authority) of the Ahl al-Bayt for divine mercy. It highlights the theological principle that Allah made it obligatory upon Himself to forgive those who call upon Him through the Prophet and his Household, emphasizing that even prolonged punishment in Hell can be terminated by this specific invocation. The narrative serves as a practical reminder of the enduring spiritual authority of the Imams in securing salvation.
